retrieval.query: SEBI permits mutual funds to avail intraday borrowings subject to specified purposes, limits tied to receivables, repayment by end of the day, board-approved policies published on AMC websites, maintenance of scheme-wise records of liquidity mismatches and sources of repayment, compliance with specified regulatory provisions, and that AMCs bear the cost or loss arising from intraday borrowing or delays in receivables. The circular is effective from September 1, 2026. Mutual Funds may avail intraday borrowings only for specified purposes (unitholder pay-outs, pay-in for investments, MTM and forex settlements, repayment of existing borrowings). The quantum of intraday borrowings shall be limited to guaranteed receivables such as inflows from RBI, Clearing Corporations, subscription inflows received in scheme bank accounts etc. The quantum of intraday borrowings shall be limited to non-guaranteed receivables sighted during the day such as inflows from maturity proceeds and/or secondary market settlement from NCDs, CP, CDs, OTC Swaps, etc. and to be received by the scheme by end of the day. AMCs may avail intraday borrowing in addition to clauses 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 solely for the purpose of meeting redemption and other pay-out to the unitholders as specified under Regulation 42(1) of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026. AMCs shall ensure that intraday borrowings are repaid by end of the day. AMCs shall ensure that any intraday borrowings converted to overnight borrowings are within regulatory limits and for the purposes allowed in Regulation 42(1) of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

regulatory_evidence.text:
2.1. Mutual Funds may avail intraday borrowings for the following purposes:
2.1.1. All unitholder pay-outs such as redemptions, IDCW pay-outs, interest etc.
2.1.2. Pay-in with respect to investments made by the scheme.
2.1.3. MTM obligations and foreign exchange settlements.
2.1.4. Repayment of existing borrowings.

2.2. The quantum of intraday borrowings shall be limited to:
2.2.1. Guaranteed receivables such as inflows from RBI, Clearing Corporations, subscription inflows received in scheme bank accounts etc.

2.2.2. Non-guaranteed receivables sighted during the day such as inflows from maturity proceedings and/or secondary market settlement from NCDs, CP, CDs, OTC Swaps, etc. and to be received by the scheme by end of the day.

2.2.3. Intraday borrowing in addition to clause 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 may be availed by AMCs solely for the purpose of meeting redemption and other pay-out to the unitholders as specified under Regulation 42(1) of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

2.3. AMCs shall be responsible for ensuring that intraday borrowings are repaid by end of the day and any intraday borrowings converted to overnight borrowings are within regulatory limits and for the purposes allowed in Regulation 42(1) of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

2.4. Boards of AMC and Trustees of a mutual fund shall approve the policy for use of intraday borrowing facility. The policy shall be made available on the website of AMC. The policy shall, inter-alia, include approval processes, monitoring mechanism etc.
2.5. AMCs shall maintain scheme wise records detailing the underlying liquidity mismatch and the expected source of repayment for the intra-day borrowing.
2.6. AMCs shall ensure compliance of clauses 6 and 7 of Fourth Schedule of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 and para 17.7 of the Master Circular.

2.7. In line with para 11.10 of the Master Circular, cost of intraday borrowing, if any, shall be borne by the AMC.  Further, any loss or cost incurred, on account of any unforeseen event or delay in receiving the funds from receivables as mentioned at clause 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 above shall also be borne by the AMC.

policy_evidence.text:
POL-001 — Scheme Borrowing and Liquidity Policy §4.1 Permitted purposes
A scheme may borrow intraday only for: (a) unit holder pay-outs such as redemptions and IDCW pay-outs; (b) pay-in for
investments made by the scheme; (c) mark-to-market obligations and foreign exchange settlements; (d) repayment of existing
borrowings.

POL-001 — Scheme Borrowing and Liquidity Policy §4.4 Approval process
Treasury raises an intraday borrowing request stating the scheme, purpose, quantum and expected source of repayment; the CFO
or a delegate approves it before drawdown. Approvals are logged in the borrowing register.

regulatory_source.title: Intraday borrowing facility availed by mutual funds

retrieval.query: SEBI directs depositories to implement a facility allowing creation of standing instructions for Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) and Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) for mutual fund units held in demat form, to be rolled out in two phases (unit‑based then amount‑based), with specific implementation and operationalization tasks and deadlines for depositories. Ensure implementation of Phase - I (Unit-based SWP/STP) by January 31, 2027 and act as nodal facilitator for implementation of this framework. Ensure implementation of Phase - II (Amount-based SWP/STP) by April 30, 2027 and act as nodal facilitator for implementation of this framework. Make the facility available for "Unit-based SWP / STP" (standing instructions based on fixed number of units to be redeemed at a specified frequency for withdrawal or for purchasing units of another scheme of the same Mutual Fund). Extend the facility to "Amount-based SWP / STP" (standing instruction for fixed amount which is required as pay-out at a specified frequency or for purchasing units of another scheme of the same Mutual Fund). Jointly publish a standard framework on depositories' websites to operationalize the facility by October 31, 2026. Make amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations for the implementation of the above framework, as may be applicable/necessary.

regulatory_evidence.text: Depositories shall be the nodal facilitator for implementation of this framework and shall ensure the implementation of Phase - I by January 31, 2027 and implementation of Phase - ll by April 30, 2027.

retrieval.query: SEBI requires persons engaged in sale/distribution of Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs) to hold the new 'NISM Series-V-D - Mutual Fund - Specialized Investment Fund Distributors Certification'; removes the mandatory requirement for 'NISM Series XIII - Common Derivatives Certification' for SIF distribution after 21 Sept 2026, provides transitional relief for holders of Series XIII obtained on/before 21 Sept 2026, and directs AMFI and AMCs to ensure compliance. Any persons employed or engaged or to be employed or engaged in the sale and/or distribution of SIF products shall be required to have a valid "NISM Series-V-D - Mutual Fund - Specialized Investment Fund Distributors Certification". Entities engaged in the sale and/or distribution of only Mutual Fund products shall continue to comply with NISM Series V-A certification, as specified under Gazette notification no. LAD -NRO/GN/2010-11/09/6422 dated May 31, 2010. The existing requirement of holding of "NISM Series XIII – Common Derivatives Certification" for the sale and/or distribution of SIF products shall not be applicable after September 21, 2026. SIF distributors holding a valid "NISM Series XIII - Common Derivatives Certification", obtained on or before September 21, 2026, shall not be required to obtain the "NISM Series -V-D – Mutual Fund - Specialized Investment Fund Distributors Certification" till the expiry of their existing "NISM Series XIII - Common Derivatives Certification"; during this period, such distributors shall continue to hold a valid "NISM Series V -A Mutual Fund Distributors Certification". AMFI and AMCs shall ensure compliance with the above requirements by distributors and agents.

regulatory_evidence.text:
21.10.1. Any persons employed or engaged or to be employed or engaged in the 

sale and/or distribution of SIF products  shall be required to have a valid 
"NISM Series-V-D - Mutual Fund - Specialized Investment Fund Distributors 
Certification". Entities holding this certification shall be eligible to distribute both 
Mutual Fund and SIF products, without separately holding "NISM Series V-A – 
Mutual Fund Distributors Certification".

21.10.3. The existing requirement of h olding of "NISM Series X III – Common 
Derivatives Certification" for the sale and/or distribution of SIF products shall not 
be applicable after September 21, 2026.

21.10.4. In order to ensure seamless transition to the new certification 
requirement, SIF distributors holding a valid "NISM Series XIII - Common 
Derivatives Certification", obtained on or before  September 21, 2026, shall not 
be required to obtain the "NISM Series -V-D – Mutual Fund - Specialized 
Investment Fund Distributors Certification" till the expiry of their existing "NISM 
Series XIII - Common Derivatives Certification". During this period, such 
distributors shall continue to hold a valid "NISM  Series V -A Mutual Fund 
Distributors Certification", as required under the erstwhile framework.

21.10.5. AMFI and AMCs shall ensure compliance with the above requirements 
by distributors and agents.

policy_evidence.text:
POL-002 — Distributor Empanelment and Certification Policy §4.2 Specialized Investment Fund strategies
Persons selling or distributing Nimbus SIF strategies must hold, in addition to NISM Series V-A, a valid NISM Series XIII
Common Derivatives Certification. Sales staff without the Series XIII certification may not discuss SIF strategies with clients.

regulatory_source.title: Certification Requirements for Distribution of Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs)

retrieval.query: SEBI requires all regulated entities to report cyber incidents promptly: by emailing mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in within 6 hours and by using SEBI's Cyber Incident Reporting Portal (https://siportal.sebi.gov.in) within 24 hours; incidents must be reported in stages (initial report, updates, and final closure) and entities must put in place systems, including amendments to bye-laws/rules/regulations as necessary, to implement these reporting requirements. Report cyber incidents to mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in within 6 hours. Report cyber incidents on the SEBI Incident Reporting Portal within 24 hours. Regulated Entities (REs) shall report cyber incidents through the Cyber Incident Reporting Portal of SEBI which can be accessed by logging into https://siportal.sebi.gov.in. Provide staged reporting on the portal: an initial report, intermediate updates as the incident evolves, and a final closure report; continue providing updates until the incident is resolved. Take necessary steps to put in place systems for implementation of this circular, including making necessary amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations, if any.
